semantics.definition: A mature cumulonimbus is rendered as one vertically connected storm body with a dark low base, a deep cauliflower-like convective tower, a fibrous or flattened anvil top, and a precipitation or virga shaft descending from the cloud. Lightning is optional, and storm severity cannot be certified from appearance alone.
paraphrase_examples: 어두운 낮은 구름 밑면에서 솟은 깊은 대류 탑이 섬유상 모루 꼭대기로 퍼지고 강수 기둥이 같은 구름에서 내려옴
contrast_examples: a dark overcast sky with a lightning graphic
a smoke plume with no connected cloud base or precipitation

match_terms: a broad dark cloud base sits low above the landscape or horizon
a massive cauliflower-textured tower rises continuously from the same cloud base
the upper cloud spreads into a flattened fibrous or striated anvil
a rain hail or virga shaft visibly descends from beneath the storm body

must_mention_any: a broad dark cloud base sits low above the landscape or horizon
a massive cauliflower-textured tower rises continuously from the same cloud base
the upper cloud spreads into a flattened fibrous or striated anvil
a rain hail or virga shaft visibly descends from beneath the storm body

obligations.instruction: Use a wide vertical frame that preserves the low dark base, full convective tower, flattened fibrous or striated anvil, and a descending precipitation shaft in one connected cloud system.

render_gates.description: A broad dark base remains connected to the cloud tower above the landscape.
A deep cauliflower-textured convective tower rises continuously from the same base.
The upper cloud visibly spreads into a flattened fibrous or striated anvil.
A precipitation or virga shaft descends from beneath the connected storm body.
Lightning, dark overcast, or smoke alone do not establish cumulonimbus structure or storm severity.
